questions.q: What is the main advantage of `lwc:if`/`lwc:elseif`/`lwc:else` over the older `if:true`/`if:false` pair?
options: lwc:if runs faster in every browser
if:true/if:false has been completely removed from the platform
lwc:if supports a multi-branch chain (if/elseif/else) in one readable structure, while if:true/if:false has no built-in else-if
lwc:if is the only directive that works with for:each
questions.explain: lwc:elseif gives a clean multi-branch chain. if:true/if:false only expresses a true/false pair directly -- expressing a third state requires stacking separate if:true/if:false blocks against different conditions.

questions.q: When should you reach for `iterator:` instead of `for:each`?
options: Whenever rendering any list at all, since iterator: is required by the compiler
iterator: and for:each are interchangeable with no functional difference
Only when the list has fewer than 10 items
Specifically when the UI needs to know whether the current item is the first or last in the list
questions.explain: iterator: exposes first and last booleans for the current item, which for:each does not provide -- that's the specific reason to choose it, for example to suppress a divider after the last row.

questions.q: Why is using an array index as a list item's `key` considered a common mistake?
options: Array indexes are not valid JavaScript values for a key attribute
Using an index as a key causes a compile-time error in every case
It works until the array is re-sorted, filtered, or has an item removed from the middle, at which point the framework can reuse the wrong DOM node for the wrong record
Keys are only required when using iterator:, not for:each
questions.explain: An index-based key breaks down as soon as the list's order or membership changes, because the framework can no longer reliably tell which rendered node corresponds to which actual record.

questions.q: In the example combining loading, empty, and populated states, why is `isEmpty` written as a getter rather than a separately tracked field?
options: A getter derived from `isLoading` and `contacts.length` can never fall out of sync with those two underlying values, unlike a separately maintained field that has to be updated manually everywhere
Getters are required by the LWC compiler for any boolean used in a template
Fields cannot be used inside lwc:if conditions at all
Getters execute on the server, which is faster for this kind of check
questions.explain: Deriving isEmpty from isLoading and contacts.length guarantees the three states stay mutually consistent, since there's only one source of truth to update. A separately tracked field would require manually keeping it in sync everywhere contacts or isLoading changes.

questions.q: Why is mixing `if:true` and `lwc:if` on the same template element not allowed?
options: It is allowed and is actually the recommended pattern for complex conditions
if:true can only be applied to component tags, never to template tags
lwc:if can only be used inside a for:each loop
A template element must use one directive family or the other, not both at once -- mixing them causes a compile error
questions.explain: The two directive families are mutually exclusive on the same element; combining if:true and lwc:if on one <template> tag is a compile-time error, not a supported pattern.
